title: What Is a Block Explorer? Check Any Crypto Transaction Yourself (Beginner Guide)
caption: Educational only. Not financial advice. How a block explorer lets you look up public crypto transactions. Plain English for beginners. AI-generated voice.

scenes.head: SENT CRYPTO. DID IT ARRIVE?
scenes.narration: You sent crypto and nothing shows up yet. How can you check what really happened?

scenes.head: BLOCK EXPLORER
scenes.narration: A block explorer is a public website that lets anyone search the records of a blockchain, and it is free to use.

scenes.head: WHAT YOU CAN LOOK UP
scenes.narration: You can search a transaction I D, or a wallet address, and see the block and the time it was recorded.

scenes.head: READ THE STATUS
scenes.narration: Pending means it is still waiting. Confirmed means it is recorded on the chain. Failed means it did not complete.

scenes.head: WHAT IT SHOWS
scenes.narration: It shows the amount, the network fee that was paid, and the addresses involved, not the names of real people.

scenes.head: STAY CAREFUL
scenes.narration: Use trusted explorers, check the web address, and never type your seed phrase into any site. A real explorer never asks.
